issues.legal_issue: A tenant becomes the deemed owner of tenanted land, extinguishing the former landowner’s interest, upon depositing the purchase price or first instalment fixed by the competent authority, unless the deposit is made while the fixing order is stayed.
material_facts: The tenant had a statutory right to purchase the tenanted land and applied to the competent authority for that purchase.
The authority fixed the purchase price and permitted payment in instalments.
The tenant deposited the first instalment fixed by the authority before the time allowed, and the order fixing the purchase price was not stayed.
The landowner’s challenge to the tenant’s purchase right had been dismissed, and the tenant’s purchase order had become final.
issues.conclusion: On deposit of the purchase price or the first instalment fixed by the Assistant Collector, the tenant became the deemed owner and the landowner ceased to have any interest in the land. A deposit made while the fixing order was stayed would not have that effect.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18(1)–(4) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, gives an eligible tenant the right to purchase, provides for determination of the land’s value and purchase price, and declares the tenant to be the owner on deposit of the purchase price or first instalment. Section 18(4)(c) permits recovery of unpaid instalments as arrears of land revenue, confirming that non-payment of a later instalment does not postpone ownership. The Court distinguished Deonandan Prashad Singh v. Ramdhari Chowdhri and Bishan Singh v. Khazan Singh, which concerned when a pre-emptor becomes owner under a pre-emption decree, not the effect of a deposit under the Tenures Act.

rule.if: statutory_tenant_purchase_proceeding and tenant_entitled_to_purchase and purchase_price_fixed_by_competent_authority and required_deposit_made and deposit_not_made_during_stay

predicates.statutory_tenant_purchase_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a tenant exercising a statutory right to purchase tenanted land.
predicates.tenant_entitled_to_purchase: The tenant qualified for the right to purchase the land.
predicates.purchase_price_fixed_by_competent_author: The competent authority determined the purchase price payable for the land.
predicates.required_deposit_made: The tenant deposited the purchase price or the first instalment fixed by the competent authority.
predicates.deposit_not_made_during_stay: The tenant made the deposit while no competent authority or court had stayed the order fixing the purchase price.

issues.definition: When a qualifying tenant makes the required deposit outside a stay, the tenant becomes the deemed owner and the former landowner loses the landowner’s interest.

issues.legal_issue: When land that a tenant was entitled to purchase is acquired before the tenant becomes its deemed owner, the landowner’s compensation entitlement is limited to the purchase price payable under the tenant’s purchase right.
material_facts: The tenant had a right to purchase the tenanted land and had applied to do so.
The acquired portion vested in the State before the tenant deposited the first instalment and became its deemed owner.
The landowner claimed compensation for the acquired portion.
The tenant’s purchase price was determinable under the statutory purchase scheme, and the landowner’s interest in the land was limited to that purchase price.
issues.conclusion: The landowner could claim compensation for the acquired land, but only to the extent of the purchase price payable by the tenant. That entitlement came from the market-value component, together with solatium and interest, and could not exceed the purchase price.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18(2) and (3) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, determines the tenant’s purchase price by a statutory measure distinct from the land’s market value on the acquisition-notification date. Under the unamended Land Acquisition Act, 1894, compensation included market value, solatium and interest, as well as specified damage components. The landowner could claim only the components reflecting the landowner’s remaining interest; that interest was limited to the purchase price. The Court rejected the view that the statutory three-fourths purchase-price calculation entitled the landowner to three-fourths of the land’s market value.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding and tenant_had_right_to_purchase and land_vested_before_tenant_became_deemed_owner and landowner_claimed_compensation

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: The proceeding concerns entitlement to compensation for land acquired by the State.
predicates.tenant_had_right_to_purchase: The tenant was entitled to purchase the land under the applicable statutory scheme.
predicates.land_vested_before_tenant_became_deemed_: The land vested in the State through acquisition before the tenant became its deemed owner.
predicates.landowner_claimed_compensation: The landowner sought compensation for the acquired land.

issues.definition: Where acquired land vested before a tenant with a purchase right became its deemed owner, the landowner’s compensation entitlement is capped at the purchase price payable by the tenant.

issues.legal_issue: A former landowner who receives compensation for land acquired after the tenant has become its deemed owner must restore the compensation to the tenant, with interest, and the unpaid debt may be charged against the former landowner’s estate.
material_facts: The tenant had deposited the required first instalment and become the deemed owner before the later acquisition of the land.
The former landowner received the compensation awarded for that land, although the tenant was entitled to it as owner.
The former landowner had the use of the compensation while the tenant was deprived of it.
The former landowner died while the appeal was pending, and the compensation had not been repaid.
issues.conclusion: The former landowner was liable to pay the compensation received to the tenant, with interest from receipt until payment. Because the former landowner had died and the amount remained unpaid, the Court declared it a debt chargeable on the deceased’s property in the hands of the legal representatives and permitted recovery through execution of the judgment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 31(2), third proviso, of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, preserves the liability of a person who receives compensation to pay it to the person lawfully entitled to it. Since the tenant had become the deemed owner before acquisition, the tenant was entitled to the compensation. The Court also required interest to account for the recipient’s use of the money while the tenant was deprived of it, and directed that the unpaid debt be chargeable against the deceased recipient’s property in the hands of the legal representatives.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding and tenant_became_deemed_owner_before_acquisition and former_landowner_received_tenant_entitled_compensation and compensation_remained_unpaid and recipient_died_before_repayment

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: The proceeding concerns compensation awarded for land acquired by the State.
predicates.tenant_became_deemed_owner_before_acquis: The tenant became the deemed owner before the acquired land vested in the State.
predicates.former_landowner_received_tenant_entitle: The former landowner received compensation to which the tenant was entitled.
predicates.compensation_remained_unpaid: The recipient had not returned the compensation to the person entitled to it.
predicates.recipient_died_before_repayment: The recipient died before repaying the compensation.

issues.definition: If a former landowner receives unpaid compensation belonging to a tenant who became owner before acquisition and dies before repayment, the compensation debt with interest is chargeable against the recipient’s estate.
